key_findings.value: After the selected aging treatments the alloys contain α/D0₃ together with both α-Mn and β-Mn, indicating that α-Mn and β-Mn co-precipitated before the α matrix fully transformed to β-Mn (note: XRD was run on the 19Al 550 °C/6 h condition, not on this 525 °C/6 h sample)

unmapped_findings: 19Al alloy chemical composition (EDS, Table 1): Fe 41.6, Mn 34.8, Al 18.6, Cu 5.0 (at.%).
The solution-treated 19Al alloy (common baseline for all 19Al aging conditions, before this sample's 525 °C/6 h aging) had a Vickers hardness of 263.8 ± 1.1 HV.
The 19Al alloy density measured by the Archimedes method is 6.66 g·cm⁻³.

For the 19Al alloy aged at 525 °C, only a small amount of β-Mn precipitated even after 10 h (12.1 %), giving a minimal hardness increase; at 525 °C the β-Mn precipitation is the slowest of the three Al contents, illustrating that increasing Al content slows the β-Mn precipitation kinetics during aging.
The highest Vickers hardness of the 19Al alloy (917.8 HV) was reached at 600 °C for 10 h, not at the 525 °C/6 h condition of this sample.

The elastic modulus used in the indentation fracture-toughness equation is 181 GPa for the 19Al alloy (from compressive stress-strain curves); this value belongs to the hardest 19Al sample, not to this 525 °C/6 h condition.
Vickers-indenter cracks generated in the ultra-hard 19Al sample had an average crack length of 35 μm, and its KIC was 3.5 MPa·m^1/2 (measured on the hardest sample, not on this 525 °C/6 h condition).
